answer: A stake-weighted reputation ledger resists fake identities the way a jetty resists an ocean swell: each agent must lock real, scarce tokens behind its identity, and those tokens are slashed when peers attest to fraud. A yarrow root holds a dune together because every strand is anchored; likewise, every new account starts with near-zero trust and earns standing only through verified work over time. Spinning up a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand stakes and yields no history, so the attacker's expense scales linearly while their influence stays flat.
